title: Not everyone who smiles at you is safe.
paragraphs: Not everyone who smiles at you is safe.

Some people don’t destroy your life loudly…
they do it quietly—while standing close enough to call you “friend.”
And here’s the part that should shake you:

Sometimes…
you’ve been that person too.
You thought it was just a vibe.

Just jokes.
Just influence.
Just “this is who I am.”

But slowly—almost invisibly—hearts get shaped.
Convictions get blurred.
Standards get lowered.
There are people who will flatter you while leading you away from truth.
People who normalize what God calls sin.
People who make darkness feel comfortable and obedience feel extreme.
And if you’re not careful, you won’t just be influenced by them—
The Bible doesn’t whisper about this. It warns you directly:

“Do not be deceived: ‘Bad company corrupts good character.’”
—1 Corinthians 15:33

That means influence is not neutral.
It is forming you—either toward Christ or away from Him.
And here’s the deeper truth most people avoid:
“Have I been toxic to someone else?”
Have I been the one who…

• Flattered instead of corrected?
• Invited people into compromise instead of holiness?
• Made sin feel small and conviction feel unnecessary?
• Used people when I needed them… then disappeared?
This is where shame starts creeping in.
But don’t run from that moment.
That moment is where conviction meets mercy.

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
—Romans 3:23

That includes the manipulator.
The compromiser.
The user.
But God doesn’t expose sin to shame you.
He exposes it to save you.
Because the same Bible that diagnoses your condition also declares your cure:

“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
—Romans 5:8

Not after you fixed yourself.
Not after you became “better.”
While you were still in it.

While you were still the one influencing wrongly.
While you were still drifting.
While you were still blind to your own damage.
This is transformation from the inside out.
Jesus didn’t come just to warn you about dangerous people.
He came to rescue you from the dangerous version of yourself.
Because at the cross, Jesus took every manipulative word, every hidden compromise, every selfish motive—
and paid for it in full.
So now, the invitation is not “feel bad.”
“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.”
This is where shame loses its power.
Because in Christ, you are not labeled by your worst influence.
You are redefined by His grace.
So before you start cutting people off…
“Lord, have I been leading people away from You instead of toward You?”
And then ask Him for something greater than better relationships—
Ask Him for a new heart.
Because when your heart changes, your influence changes.
You stop being the one who pulls people into compromise…
…and you become the one who pulls people into Christ.
Right now, this is your moment.
If the Holy Spirit is pressing on your heart, don’t resist it.
Pray this in your own words:

“Lord Jesus, open my eyes.
Show me where I’ve been wrong.
Cleanse my heart.
Change my influence.
Make me someone who leads others closer to You, not away from You.
I surrender.”
